title: Edge peering degradation: root cause hypotheses & verification checklist
body:
Executive summary:

On 2025-02-17 between ~12:15-14:40 UTC we observed elevated 5xx rates and increased p95/p99 write latencies from a subset of EU edge POPs serving customers in eu-west1 and eu-central1. Symptoms included: origin request timeouts from CDN -> regional origin, asymmetric traceroutes from monitoring probes, and intermittent BGP path changes visible in public route collectors. Traffic volume was normal; CPU and GPU capacity on backends were healthy.

Primary impact:
- Short bursts of 502/504s for generation endpoints for a small percentage (~2-5%) of requests originating in Central/Eastern Europe.
- Increased tail latency on streaming sessions (clients observed stalls ~1-3s).

Investigation notes (quick):
- CDN edge health checks showed origin connect timeouts coincident with BGP path flaps reported by our ISP.
- Synthetic probes from multiple providers (RIPE Atlas, internal probes) showed path divergence: some probes reached origin via direct interconnect, others via transit with high AS path length and packet loss.
- Our regional egress via ISP-X had a partial peering disruption; however some ISP-X routes remained stable via alternate IXHs.
- Internal routing (VPC->NAT) looked normal; no misconfiguration changes in our infra teams.

Timeline (high level):
- 12:10 UTC: first automated alerts (p95 spikes) from EU edge dashboards.
- 12:15-12:30: on-call started gathering telemetry; escalated to on-call SRE and network lead (Sanjay).
- 12:35: CDN metrics show origin connect errors rising; origin host DNS resolution OK.
- 12:45: packet captures on border routers show increased TCP retransmits and ICMP unreachable on some peering links.
- 13:05: mitigation attempt #1: increase CDN origin retries and small client-side backoff (config change). Reduced 5xx rate modestly.
- 13:25: mitigation attempt #2: weight shift of traffic away from affected POPs via CDN control plane (soft shift, 10-20% increments). Observed improvement over 20 minutes.
- 14:20: traffic stabilized; ISP-X confirmed a partial peering restoration; full closure 14:40 after route convergence.

Hypotheses (rank-ordered):
1) Upstream peering degradation at ISP-X caused path asymmetry and packet loss to our regional origins, increasing origin connect timeouts. Evidence: public BGP collectors, ISP-X status update, packet loss on border interfaces.
2) CDN origin health probes were too sensitive to transient packet loss and caused origin flaps in the CDN control plane (health check threshold + low retry policy). Evidence: origin probe timeouts preceding 502s, quick reduction after increasing retries.
3) Border router interface errors due to microbursts triggered local retransmits and contributed to latency spikes. Evidence: ifInErrors/ifOutErrors increase on single border port; logs ambiguous.
4) A small config change in a rollout window (unrelated service) created a coincidentity but not causal — low likelihood.

Verification checklist (what to run next time / when reproducing):
- Check public BGP collectors (RouteViews, RIPE) for AS path changes for prefixes serving our origins. Commands: 
  - bgpmon/looking glass links + RIPE RIS dumps (link in Confluence doc).
- Run traceroute/mtr from multiple vantage points (AWS eu-west1, GCP europe-west, RIPE Atlas) to origin IPs and CDN edge hostnames. Capture for comparison.
- Collect tcpdump on border routers and on origin hosts (short windows aligned with alerts). Save PCAPs with timestamps.
- Correlate CDN control plane origin health events (timestamps) with BGP changes and packet loss windows.
- Inspect NAT gateway and border interface error counters (ifInErrors/ifOutErrors, drops).
- Reproduce origin connection with curl from edge test host: curl -v --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 20 https://origin-host.example.internal/health

Immediate mitigations (operator checklist):
- If origin connect errors correlate with ISP peering: request ISP peering status and request either a reroute or announce via alternate IXs.
- CDN: temporarily raise origin health check thresholds and increase retry/backoff to avoid origin flapping during transient network loss. Document exact config keys in this doc.
- Edge traffic steering: perform a gradual weight shift away from affected POPs (10% increments every 5–10 minutes) and monitor 5xx and latency.
- If border interface shows sustained hardware errors: escalate to netops to bring up backup port and migrate sessions.

Sample operator commands (notes to self):
- traceroute: traceroute -n -w 2 -q 1 <origin-ip>
- mtr (short): mtr -r -c 50 -w <origin-ip>
- tcpdump on border: sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host <edge-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/edge-<ts>.pcap (rotate every 2m)
- check CDN: curl -XGET "https://cdn-api.example/v1/origins/<origin-id>/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CDN_TOKEN"
- check if counters: ssh borderrouter; show interfaces counters | grep -E "ifInErrors|ifOutErrors"

Observability gaps uncovered (to address):
- No automated correlation of BGP collector alerts with CDN origin health events (we saw them manually). Create a pipeline to correlate and page network owner when both spike.
- Limited edge-level packet capture retention; emergency capture took manual ops and missed early minutes. Implement ring buffer capture for border interfaces (short-term, 15–30m).
- CDN control plane health thresholds are conservative for brief network glitches; we need a documented origin-sensitivity profile and per-region knob.

Long-term actions / proposed tickets (owners assigned):
- SRE-4123 (assigned Sanjay): Build BGP->CDN correlation alerting (confluence draft linked).
- SRE-4124 (assigned Leah): Implement ring-buffer packet capture on border routers + automated upload to secure S3 on trigger.
- SRE-4125 (assigned Marta): Review CDN origin probe defaults; implement region-aware retry/backoff profiles.
- SRE-4126 (assigned Ethan): Add synthetic traceroute job from 10 vantage points for all regions, store results and diff on each alert.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Was any third-party CDN partner peering change (they did a configuration push at ~11:50 UTC)? Need confirmation from CDN partner.
- Can we safely raise origin probe thresholds for all customers? Need product input on acceptable error surface.
- Do we have legal/network constraints to request immediate alternate peering from ISP-X during incidents?

Notes for the postmortem meeting:
- Bring packet captures, CDN origin event logs, BGP collector snapshots, and the timeline above.
- Target outcomes: 1) decide threshold for automated correlation alert; 2) short-term origin probe profile change; 3) action plan for ring-buffer capture rollout.

Related artifacts / links: see linked_artifacts above.

Quick operator TL;DR (copy for on-call playbook):
1) Check CDN origin health events and BGP collector for prefixes serving origin.
2) If both show anomalies, raise CDN origin retries + gradual weight shift away from affected POPs.
3) If border interface errors present, move traffic to alternate interconnect and engage netops.

Notes to self (informal):
- This felt like a classic upstream peering flake amplified by sensitive origin health checks. Next time I want the correlation automated so we don't chase infra that looks normal.
- We should add a short runbook appendix that lists exactly where to flip CDN origin retry and how to do weighted shifts in the CDN control plane (ops steps + screenshots).

Document history:
- 2025-02-17 initial notes and timeline (Ava)
- 2025-02-18 added hypotheses and sample commands (Sanjay)
- 2025-02-20 appended mitigation results and next steps (Leah)
- 2025-03-02 draft updated with ticket numbers and owners (Ava)
